memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting." - Lev 1:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Exodus ended with a problem. The tabernacle was finished, the glory of the LORD filled it, and Moses could not enter (Ex 40:35). God had come near, but nobody could come near Him. Leviticus opens by answering that problem in its very first sentence: God called.

Notice who speaks first. Moses is not searching for God. Moses is not climbing a mountain this time. God calls him from inside the tent. The whole book that follows — all the offerings, all the blood, all the careful instructions — is God telling His people how they may come to Him. It is not a book about how to earn God's attention. It is a book written because God already gave it.

Many of us carry a quiet fear that God is silent, or worse, that He is waiting for us to make the first move. Leviticus says otherwise. Holiness did not make God distant; it made Him speak. And He is still the God who speaks first. He spoke fully and finally in His Son (Heb 1:1-2), and through Christ the way into His presence stands open (Heb 10:19-22).

Before you read another word of Leviticus, hear this: God wanted to be approached.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I picture God as reluctant to be approached, or as the One who calls first?
2. Where in my life am I waiting for God to speak, when He has already spoken in Scripture?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You spoke first and did not leave me guessing how to come to You. Open my ears as I read, and open my heart to the Son through whom I now draw near. Amen.
